commit.message:
Keep a call's request and reply charges apart

A call holds its request charge from the batch handoff until the node
answers, and its reply charge until the reply is sent or reset, so a
deadline can no longer drop a charge the node still holds or leak one.
A call whose deadline passed before its batch goes out stays out.
Complete pushes onto a lock-free list instead of taking a mutex.

@@ -203,7 +203,7 @@ Cost on this host (aarch64, 8 cores): about 80 ms per run of one seed, so 64 see
 
 Each connection has a reader goroutine, which decodes frames and copies each request message once out of the Framer into a buffer of its own size, and a writer goroutine, which is the only one that writes and which keeps to the client's flow-control windows. A streaming call runs in a goroutine from its first headers. Status and MemberList run in a goroutine of their own.
 
-The unary calls that the node runs (KV, Compact and the unary Lease calls) take the whole-batch path. The reader decodes each complete request and hands all of them to the committer with one `Node.SubmitBatch` call. It does this when reading the next frame could wait for the client, because that frame is not buffered whole or starts a header block that continues in later frames, or at 256 requests or 4 MiB. There is no timer. The committer submits each request to the core, and after each `Process` it hands every connection all of its replies of that turn with one `Complete` call. `Complete` only appends under a lock of its own and wakes the writer, which encodes the replies. So such a call costs no goroutine, context, channel or inbox send of its own. Each call holds its request bytes plus 512 until its reply is sent, and its reply bytes from when the node answers. Once a connection's calls hold more than 64 MiB, its receive window is not credited back, so the client stops sending while the reader still reads pings, resets and window updates. If the node stops, every call it held fails with "server stopped" after the replies it already gave are sent. Response header and trailer blocks are HPACK literals that are never indexed, each after a dynamic table size update to 0, so they are built once and are valid whatever table size the client set. The server follows grpc-go and etcd where clients can see it:
+The unary calls that the node runs (KV, Compact and the unary Lease calls) take the whole-batch path. The reader decodes each complete request and hands all of them to the committer with one `Node.SubmitBatch` call. It does this when reading the next frame could wait for the client, because that frame is not buffered whole or starts a header block that continues in later frames, or at 256 requests or 4 MiB. There is no timer. The committer submits each request to the core, and after each `Process` it hands every connection all of its replies of that turn with one `Complete` call. `Complete` only pushes them onto a lock-free list and wakes the writer, which encodes the replies. So such a call costs no goroutine, context, channel or inbox send of its own. Each call holds its request bytes plus 512 from when the reader hands it over until the node answers, and its reply bytes from then until the reply is sent or the client resets the call. A call whose deadline passed before its batch goes out is not handed over. Once a connection's calls hold more than 64 MiB, its receive window is not credited back, so the client stops sending while the reader still reads pings, resets and window updates. If the node stops, every call it held fails with "server stopped" after the replies it already gave are sent. Response header and trailer blocks are HPACK literals that are never indexed, each after a dynamic table size update to 0, so they are built once and are valid whatever table size the client set. The server follows grpc-go and etcd where clients can see it:
 
 - The receive limit is etcd's 1.5 MiB request limit plus 512 KiB, with grpc-go's ResourceExhausted "received message larger than max". Compressed messages are refused with Unimplemented.
 - `grpc-timeout` ends the call with DeadlineExceeded when it passes, whether or not the request is complete or the handler started; `0n` has passed already. etcd's `hasleader` metadata fails a call without a leader with "etcdserver: no leader", unary calls included, and ends a Watch or LeaseKeepAlive stream after three checks one second apart find no leader, as etcd's interceptors do.
